SUCCESSOR F24 (WHY PHASE B FAILED, and it was MINE): the last recorded body walk went 17,929 m of a 3,206 m journey, took 111 simulated minutes, finished 592 m short and NEVER ABORTED — longest_stuck_frames 0, mired_frames 0. It was not stuck, it was busy. Cause found offline without a browser: plan.path is the navigator TRACE, every position it stood at INCLUDING the places it stopped and turned 108 degrees to read a post. Around waypoint 814 the trace runs z 4820.1 -> 4823.0 -> 4825.7 -> 4828.6 -> 4824.2 -> 4821.3, doubling back through ~8 m. Engine.walkPath advances to the next waypoint only once the body is within lookahead_m (4.5 m) OF THAT WAYPOINT, so a trace that reverses inside the lookahead makes the follower walk backwards, re-acquire and walk forwards again, indefinitely. Fixed in MY probe, not in walkPath (which other probes share): tidyPath() does bounded loop removal before phase B — from each kept point, jump to the LAST point within 7 m inside a 60-point window, which is the shape a recorded turn-on-the-spot makes and not a shape a road makes. MEASURED: 1035 trace points / 3206 m -> 506 route points / 3091 m, i.e. it removed 115 m (3.6%) and ZERO sharp reversals (>120 deg) remain. Both lengths are reported in phase_b_route so a reader can refuse the run if the tidy ever takes real distance instead of dither.
